headline: Highest risk is medium: pdf.js can feed Superset with unverified PDF-derived content, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and runs in a browser-based worker model, while Superset consumes API-driven analytics content. If pdf.js output is copied or piped into Superset workflows, attacker-controlled PDF text could be treated as instructions or trusted content. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into Superset dashboards, SQL snippets, or notes without sanitization
IF Superset renders or reuses PDF-extracted text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any PDF-derived text enters Superset
Strip markup and instruction-like phrases from extracted text
Use a separate staging workspace for PDF outputs
Disable copy-paste bridges between the tools during ingestion
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to extracted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and has no network egress, while Superset has allowlisted network egress and API calls. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or sensitive data classes on Superset, so leakage is possible only through operator-mediated transfer and appears limited.
conditions: IF PDF documents contain sensitive data and are manually pasted or uploaded into Superset
IF Superset is configured to export or sync those inputs to external services
mitigations: Keep PDF processing and BI workspaces separate
Avoid uploading PDF contents into Superset unless necessary
Review Superset outbound destinations before use
Redact sensitive fields before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and writes only PDF files, while Superset exposes API calls and allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is not evidenced. Any contention would require an external orchestrator or shared storage not present here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or API-backed dataset
IF an external orchestrator lacks locking or conflict resolution
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces or datasets
Serialize writes through one operator
Check for duplicate edits before syncing
Use read-only exports from pdf.js
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted text from PDFs, and Superset can consume API-backed analytics content. If Superset treats pdf.js output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors or malicious PDF content can cascade into dashboards, reports, or downstream actions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Superset ingests PDF-extracted text without validation
IF downstream reports or queries are generated from that unverified text
mitigations: Require human verification of extracted facts
Compare extracted values against the source PDF
Mark PDF-derived fields as untrusted in Superset
Limit automated actions from imported content
requires-engineering: add validation rules for imported fields

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, residency constraints, or retention-policy mismatches. pdf.js touches PDF documents locally and has no secrets or OAuth scopes; Superset lists no data classes touched. With no documented regulated-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either tool
IF a deployment policy assigns conflicting residency or retention rules
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Classify any regulated PDFs before ingestion
Review retention settings in Superset
Keep regulated data out of the pair unless approved
